parts.name: D00038 Board
parts.reasoning: The object appears to be a shallow rectangular serving tray/platter with rounded edges and a raised lip. No product dimensions are provided, so I estimate a typical size of roughly 0.28–0.32 m long, 0.18–0.22 m wide, and 0.025–0.035 m tall. The glossy white finish and rounded molded form are consistent with glazed ceramic/porcelain; if the asset is known to be molded plastic, mass and density should be reduced substantially. For a ceramic tray, the actual material density is about 2200–2400 kg/m^3, but the object is hollow/shallow rather than a solid box. Estimating a base thickness of about 4–6 mm plus a raised rim around the perimeter gives an actual ceramic volume on the order of 0.00025–0.00040 m^3, resulting in a mass around 0.55–0.95 kg. I choose 0.75 kg as a reasonable midpoint for a small-to-medium glazed ceramic tray. The dominant contact surface is smooth glazed ceramic, so friction is lower than rubber or unfinished wood but higher than polished glass; static friction around 0.35 and dynamic friction around 0.28 are appropriate for ceramic on common lab/table surfaces. Restitution is kept modest at 0.35 because ceramic is hard but the tray shape and contact damping reduce usable bounce; also, fragile ceramics should generally not be simulated as highly elastic. For Isaac Sim / PhysX, a convex hull would overfill the recessed center but is adequate if only outer contact stability is needed. For more accurate tray interactions, use convex decomposition with several simple convex parts: bottom slab plus four rim segments and rounded-corner approximations. SDF mesh collision can be used for high-fidelity contact with the recessed bowl-like region, but it is more expensive and best reserved for cases where small objects must rest inside the tray. Contact offset of 0.003 m and rest offset of 0.0005 m are suitable for a centimeter-scale hard object, avoiding visual interpenetration while maintaining stable contacts. CCD is not required for normal quasi-static placement but is enabled here as a safe default if the tray may be dropped or moved quickly. Gravity uses the standard Isaac Sim scene vector [0, 0, -9.81]. Compliant contacts are set with high stiffness and moderate damping only to regularize hard ceramic contact; the object itself should still be treated as rigid and non-deformable. Since this is a single rigid tray with no joints, articulation parameters are effectively unused.
